mainTopic: Testing the views of רב מתנא (30 days) and בר פדא (29 days) on the length of a plain נזירות against several משניות
overview: The משנה says that someone who takes two terms of נזירות shaves for the first on day 31 and for the second on day 61. But if he shaved the first on day 30, he shaves the second on day 60. The first half fits רב מתנא, who holds a plain נזירות lasts 30 days. בר פדא, who holds it lasts 29 days, explains that the first half is about someone who said 'thirty full days,' and that the second half supports him. רב מתנא explains the second half by saying day 30 counts for both terms. The גמרא then asks why the משנה repeats the idea of מקצת היום ככולו. It answers that we might have thought the idea works for one term of נזירות but not for two. Next, a משנה says shaving on day 59 after two terms is valid because day 30 counts. That line seems unneeded for בר פדא, but he answers that this line is his very source. Finally, a משנה says a נזיר who becomes טמא on day 30 loses his whole count. That fits רב מתנא but is hard for בר פדא, and the answer comes on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The first half of the משנה seems to contradict בר פדא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges בר פדא from the first half of the משנה, which says to shave on day 31 and day 61.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to בר פדא, this is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just showed that the first half of the משנה fits רב מתנא. Now it challenges בר פדא: if a נזירות is only 29 days, why does the משנה say to shave on day 31?
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר פדא holds that a plain נזירות lasts 29 days, so the shaving should be on day 30. The משנה's numbers, 31 and 61, match a 30-day term. That looks like a direct problem for בר פדא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; a challenge
But / however (turns to the other opinion)

phrases.english: But according to bar Padda, it is difficult!
phrases.notes: The difficulty is the משנה's opening rule: shave on day 31 for the first term and day 61 for the second.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the earlier observation that the first half fits רב מתנא to ask about בר פדא
steps.kashyaTarget: בר פדא's view that a plain נזירות lasts 29 days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's first half sets shaving on days 31 and 61, which only fits 30-day terms.

steps.title: בר פדא: the second half supports me, and the first half is about 'full' days
steps.stepSummary: בר פדא points to the second half of the משנה, which says to shave on days 30 and 60, as support. He explains the first half as a case where the person said 'thirty full days.'
steps.simpleTranslation: בר פדא would tell you: look at the second half of the משנה. 'If he shaved for the first term on day 30, he shaves for the second on day 60.' So the second half supports me. The first half is about someone who said 'complete' days.
steps.whatsHappening: בר פדא answers the challenge. He shows that the end of the משנה matches his view, and he limits the beginning of the משנה to a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shaving on days 30 and 60 makes sense if each term is 29 days. That is exactly בר פדא's view. The first half, with 31 and 61, is pushed into a case where the person said 'thirty full days.' Then each term really is 30 days.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read) the last part of the משנה
The last part of a משנה or ברייתא
The first part of a משנה or ברייתא
Supports him
Complete / full (days)

steps.confusionAlert: For בר פדא, a plain term is 29 days, but if someone says 'thirty full days,' it is 30. The first half of the משנה is about that special wording, not about a plain נזירות.

phrases.english: Bar Padda could say to you:
Read the last part of the mishna:

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם גִּילַּח אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה לְיוֹם שְׁלֹשִׁים —
phrases.english: And if he shaved for the first term on the thirtieth day,
he shaves for the second term on the sixtieth day.
Rather, the last part supports him,
and the first part is about one who says 'complete' days.
phrases.notes: He means someone who said he would be a נזיר for thirty full days, so each term really is 30 days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ בַּר פְּדָא, אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against בר פדא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) of the first half, plus support from the second half
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first half of the משנה, with days 31 and 61, describes a plain נזירות and goes against בר פדא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second half describes a plain נזירות of 29 days. The first half is about someone who said 'thirty full days.'

steps.title: The second half of the משנה seems to contradict רב מתנא
steps.stepSummary: Now the גמרא turns the question around: the second half of the משנה, with days 30 and 60, seems to go against רב מתנא's 30-day view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רב מתנא, the last part of the משנה is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges רב מתנא from the same second half that just helped בר פדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מתנא holds a plain נזירות is 30 days, so the shaving should be on day 31 and day 61. The second half allows shaving on days 30 and 60. That seems to assume shorter, 29-day terms.

phrases.english: And according to Rav Mattana, the last part is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the second half, just read in favor of בר פדא, against רב מתנא
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מתנא's view that a plain נזירות lasts 30 days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Shaving on days 30 and 60 looks like 29-day terms, which goes against a 30-day view.

steps.title: רב מתנא: day thirty counts for both terms
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנא explains the second half using the משנה's own words: day 30 counts as the last day of the first term and also the first day of the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנא would tell you: it is as the last part of the משנה itself teaches. Day 30 counts for this term and for that term.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנא answers the challenge by quoting the end of the משנה. Day 30 is shared by both terms, so the numbers still work with 30-day terms.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Part of day 30 counts as a full day, so the first term is finished on that day and he may shave. The same day 30 also counts as day 1 of the second term. So the second term's 30 days end on day 59, and he shaves on day 60. Both terms are still 30 days each.

keyTerms.meaning: As it teaches
Counts for this and for that (for both)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה can fit both views. For בר פדא, the second half describes a plain 29-day נזירות. For רב מתנא, it works because day 30 is shared by both terms.

phrases.english: Rav Mattana could say to you:
It is as the last part teaches:
The thirtieth day counts for this and for that.
phrases.notes: He means day 30 is both the last day of the first term and the first day of the second.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב מַתְנָא, כִּדְקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רב מתנא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the case through a rule stated in the same משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Shaving on days 30 and 60 means each term is only 29 days.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each term is 30 days, but day 30 counts for both terms, so shaving on days 30 and 60 works.

steps.title: Why repeat the rule that part of a day counts as a whole day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the last part of the משנה adds. The idea of מקצת היום ככולו was already taught earlier in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this teaching? That part of the day is like the whole day? But it already said that once!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה for repeating itself. It already taught that part of a day counts as a full day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that day 30 can count shows that a part of a day counts as a full day. The משנה already taught this idea in an earlier line, so the second time seems unnecessary. The גמרא wants to know what new thing it teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: Part of a day counts like the whole day
One time (already)
What is it (what does it teach)?

phrases.english: What is it teaching, that part of the day is like all of it?
But he already said it once!
phrases.notes: This points back to an earlier line of the same משנה, which already taught this idea.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי הִיא, מִקְצָת הַיּוֹם כְּכוּלּוֹ? הָא אַמְרַהּ חֲדָא זִימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב מתנא's reading and asks why the משנה needs that line at all
steps.kashyaTarget: The last part of the משנה ('day thirty counts for both')
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה does not repeat itself for no reason, and מקצת היום ככולו was already taught.

steps.title: The repetition teaches that the rule works even across two terms
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we might have thought מקצת היום ככולו works only inside one term of נזירות. The משנה teaches that it also works across two terms.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: this applies only to one נזירות, but not to two. So the משנה teaches us that it applies to two as well.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the repeat is needed. It teaches something new: one day can be split between two terms of נזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier line only showed that part of day 30 counts toward finishing a single term. Here, the same day does two jobs: it ends one term and starts another. Without this line, we might have thought one day cannot serve two terms.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (what we would have thought)
These words apply (only to this case)
A term of being a נזיר
It teaches us (the new point)

steps.whatToRemember: מקצת היום ככולו works even across two terms of נזירות. The same day 30 can end the first term and begin the second.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a single day can be counted twice, for two separate terms, and not just used once.

phrases.english: You might have said:
this applies only to one term of naziriteship,
but to two terms of naziriteship, no;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about why the משנה repeats itself
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: the repeat is needed to block a wrong idea
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מקצת היום ככולו works only within a single term of נזירות.
steps.terutzMaskana: מקצת היום ככולו works even across two terms, so one day can end one term and begin the next.

steps.title: Why would the משנה need to say that day 30 counts?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: a person with two terms of נזירות who shaved on day 59 has done his duty, because day 30 counts toward his total. This fits רב מתנא, but for בר פדא it seems obvious and unneeded.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: If he shaved on day sixty minus one, he has done his duty, because day thirty counts in his total. For רב מתנא this works well. But for בר פדא, why do I need this line? He already said a plain term is thirty minus one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new משנה about a person who took on two terms of נזירות. It shows that the משנה's reason fits רב מתנא but seems unneeded for בר פדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב מתנא, each term is 30 days. Shaving on day 59 works only if day 30 counts for both terms, using מקצת היום ככולו, so the משנה has to teach it. For בר פדא, the first term ends after day 29, so day 30 is simply the first day of the second term, and there seems to be nothing new to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: It counts toward his number of days
It is fine for... (it works for one side)
It works out well
Why do I need this? (it seems unneeded)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question of 'the משנה goes against בר פדא.' The question is softer: for בר פדא the line seems to say something obvious, so why would the משנה bother saying it?

phrases.english: We learned in a משנה: If he shaved
phrases.notes: This is about someone who took on two terms of נזירות in a row.

phrases.english: on day sixty minus one, he has done his duty,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיּוֹם שְׁלֹשִׁים עוֹלֶה לוֹ מִן הַמִּנְיָן.
phrases.english: because day thirty counts in his total.
For רב מתנא, this works well.
But for בר פדא, why do I need this line?
He already said a plain term is thirty minus one!
phrases.notes: For him day 30 is already free to be the first day of the second term, so the line looks obvious.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַב מַתְנָא נִיחָא אֶלָּא לְבַר פְּדָא לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the question about the first משנה, the גמרא tests the two views against a new משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: בר פדא's view that a plain נזירות is 29 days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the first term ends after day 29, then day 30 naturally belongs to the second term, so the משנה's reason 'day 30 counts' seems unneeded.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shaving on day 59 after two terms is valid because day 30 counts in the total.

steps.title: בר פדא: This line is my source
steps.stepSummary: בר פדא answers that this line of the משנה is not unneeded. It is exactly the source he leans on for his 29-day view.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would say to you: I too rely on this line.
steps.whatsHappening: בר פדא answers the question. He says the line of the משנה is the very source for his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed בר פדא's 29-day rule came from somewhere else, which made the משנה's line look extra. בר פדא flips it: the משנה says day 59 is enough for two terms, and that only adds up simply if each term is 29 days. So the line is his proof, not something extra.

keyTerms.meaning: He would say to you (the גמרא answers for him)
I too
I rely on this (this is my source)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָךְ: אֲנָא נָמֵי אַהָא סְמַכִי.
phrases.english: He would say to you: I too rely on this.
phrases.notes: He means: this line of the משנה is where I learned that a plain term is 29 days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ אֲנָא נָמֵי אַהָא סְמַכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 for בר פדא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The line that looked extra is really the source of the view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought בר פדא already knew the 29-day rule, so the משנה's line added nothing for him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's line is the source of בר פדא's 29-day rule, so it is needed.

steps.title: Becoming טמא on day 30 cancels everything
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another משנה: a person who said 'I am a נזיר' and became טמא on day 30 loses his whole count. This fits רב מתנא, but it is hard for בר פדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: Someone who said 'I am a נזיר' and became טמא on day thirty, it cancels everything. For רב מתנא this works well, but for בר פדא it is hard!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another משנה as a challenge to בר פדא, ending with a clear 'it is hard' for him. The גמרא's answer for him comes on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב מתנא, day 30 is still inside the term, so becoming טמא then ruins the whole count, just as the משנה says. For בר פדא, the term ended after day 29, so on day 30 he is already finished. Why would טומאה then cancel everything?

keyTerms.meaning: He became טמא (ritually impure)
It cancels the whole count, and he must start again
It is a difficulty

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a stronger challenge than step 7. There the line only looked extra for בר פדא; here the ruling itself seems to go against his view.

phrases.english: We learned in a משנה: Someone who said, 'I am a נזיר,'

phrases.aramaic: נִטְמָא יוֹם שְׁלֹשִׁים — סוֹתֵר אֶת הַכֹּל.
phrases.english: and became טמא on day thirty, it cancels everything.
For רב מתנא, this works well,
but for בר פדא it is hard!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַב מַתְנָא נִיחָא אֶלָּא לְבַר פְּדָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After answering one question for בר פדא, the גמרא brings a new and stronger challenge from another משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: בר פדא's view that a plain נזירות is 29 days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the term ends after day 29, becoming טמא on day 30 happens after the נזירות is done and should not cancel it. Yet the משנה says it cancels everything.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A plain נזיר who becomes טמא on day 30 loses his whole count.
